hints: Look first at the four outer arrows in each diagram and ask, should blood be entering the top thin-walled atria or leaving the bottom thick-walled ventricles?

Remember the golden rule: vena cava fills right atrium and pulmonary veins fill left atrium, while blood must leave via the pulmonary artery on the right and the aorta on the left, always moving atrium to ventricle inside.
walkthrough:
**Orientate yourself on the heart**

The heart in the diagram is facing you, so your left is the anatomical right side. The thin-walled top chambers are the atria which fill, and the thick-walled bottom chambers are the ventricles which pump out.

Rule to use:
$$atrium \rightarrow ventricle \rightarrow artery$$

**Check the correct in and out pattern**

On the anatomical right (your left), deoxygenated blood must come IN via the vena cava to the right atrium and go OUT via the pulmonary artery to the lungs. On the anatomical left (your right), oxygenated blood must come IN via the pulmonary veins to the left atrium and go OUT via the aorta to the body.

**Match to the diagrams**

Only diagram B shows both atria filling and both ventricles emptying correctly, with inside arrows also going up from atrium to ventricle. The other diagrams reverse one or both sides, so B is the only possible flow.

options.A: Right side is correct but left side is reversed, showing blood entering via the aorta and leaving via the pulmonary veins, which is impossible.
options.B: Shows vena cava into right atrium and pulmonary artery out, plus pulmonary veins into left atrium and aorta out, with both internal flows atrium to ventricle. This is the correct double circulation.
options.C: Shows blood leaving the atria and entering the ventricles via the great arteries, so all four outer arrows on the vena cava, pulmonary artery, aorta and pulmonary veins are the wrong way.
options.D: Left side is correct but right side is reversed, showing blood leaving via the vena cava and entering via the pulmonary artery, which is backwards.
